steps.title: Pushbuttons
steps.markdownContent:
### Anatomical Tour of the Tactile Pushbutton
Grab a 4-pin momentary tactile pushbutton from your kit. These tiny buttons are built into robots, game controllers, and appliances worldwide.

### The 4-Pin Mystery: Why Four Legs for Two Contacts?
When you look at the bottom of the button, you notice **4 metal legs**, but a simple switch only needs 2 wires to connect. Why are there 4?

Inside the plastic housing:
- The two legs on the **same long side** are permanently joined together by an internal metal bar!
- Leg A and Leg B are connected to each other inside.
- Leg C and Leg D are connected to each other inside.
- The push action connects the AB pair to the CD pair!

```
Top View of 4-Pin Tactile Button:

   Pin 1 [=== Internal Bar ===] Pin 2
                |  |
             [ Switch ]
                |  |
   Pin 3 [=== Internal Bar ===] Pin 4
```

### Breadboard Insertion Technique
To prevent shorting the switch out before you even push it, always insert the button so its body **straddles the center divider trench (ravine)** of your solderless breadboard:
1. Place Pins 1 and 2 on Row 15, Column D and E (left side of ravine).
2. Place Pins 3 and 4 on Row 15, Column F and G (right side of ravine).
3. Press firmly until all four legs seat cleanly into the breadboard spring clips.
4. Press down with your index finger: feel the crisp tactile snap as the miniature metal dome clicks inside!

quickCheck.question: Why do solderless breadboards feature a center divider trench (ravine)?
options: To electrically isolate opposing rows so dual-pin parts do not short together
To store extra jumper wires during assembly
To act as a heat sink for the power supply
quickCheck.explanation: The center trench separates columns a-e from f-j, allowing DIP chips and buttons to straddle across without shorting.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Breadboard rows are connected across columns a-e and f-j, but separated by the center ravine.

quickCheck.question: What happens when you release your finger from a momentary pushbutton?
options: An internal flexible spring snaps the contacts apart, opening the circuit
The switch remains locked closed permanently
The polarity of the connected battery reverses
quickCheck.explanation: Momentary switches only maintain contact while external force is applied; releasing them opens the circuit.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Momentary pushbuttons return to their open state as soon as pressure is released.

questions.question: What does Normally Open (NO) mean for a momentary pushbutton?
options: Contacts are disconnected until your finger presses down
questions.explanation: Normally Open buttons only conduct current while actively held down!

questions.question: Why do tactile pushbuttons have 4 pins?
options: To provide mechanical stability on breadboards with two internal pairs
Because each pin needs its own battery
questions.explanation: The 4 legs provide firm stability and duplicate pins in pairs!
